paper.title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation
paper.tldr: N nanoAstra is introduced, an approach to training vision-language models for generalizable manipulation that combines semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning (CP-SFT) and represents robot behavior as semantic steps composed of reusable, parameterized action primitives, guided by explicit progress descriptions.

paper.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
paper.tldr: This work proposes a simple modification to recover the original formulation of weight decay regularization by decoupling the weight decay from the optimization steps taken w.r.t. the loss function, and provides empirical evidence that this modification substantially improves Adam's generalization performance.

paper.tldr: A new model based onpi 0.5 is described that uses co-training on heterogeneous tasks to enable broad generalization and is demonstrated for the first time that an end-to-end learning-enabled robotic system can perform long-horizon and dexterous manipulation skills, such as cleaning a kitchen or bedroom, in entirely new homes.

paper.tldr: First-place systems for all four evaluated AlexandriaX-2026 settings are reported: both English-to-dialect translation tracks, cross-dialect translation, and translation-error detection, with candidate-constrained MBR beating the strongest complete candidate in all 13 dialects and gaining 1.2554 macro spBLEU overall.

paper.title: COMET-22: Unbabel-IST 2022 Submission for the Metrics Shared Task
paper.tldr: The joint contribution of Unbabel and IST to the WMT 2022 Metrics Shared Task is presented and both submissions show improved correlations compared to state-of-the-art metrics from last year as well as increased robustness to critical errors.

paper.title: Improving Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding with Multi-Prompt
paper.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
paper.tldr: This work shows multi-prompt improves MBR across a comprehensive set of conditional generation tasks, and shows this is a result of estimating a more diverse and higher quality candidate space than that of a single prompt.

paper.title: A Call for Clarity in Reporting BLEU Scores
paper.tldr: Pointing to the success of the parsing community, it is suggested machine translation researchers settle upon the BLEU scheme, which does not allow for user-supplied reference processing, and provide a new tool, SACREBLEU, to facilitate this.
